result.lens: Injection and code execution: every path from data this system does not control (OData HTTP response bodies, recorded fixtures, file paths outside the repo, subprocess output) to something that executes or is interpreted — subprocess, urlopen, SQL emission/execution, YAML loading, sqlfluff, and file writes.
consideredAndRejected: subprocess.run in src/adss/engine.py:82 — argument list is [str(self.binary), *arguments, '--no-tui'] with no shell=True. self.binary is Project.engine_binary (a fixed repo-relative path) and *arguments is only ever the literals 'install'/'--connection'/'dev'/'deploy'/'execute' passed from src/adss/cli.py:214, 222, 231. No HTTP body, fixture value, or filename reaches an argv element. The binary is additionally sha256-verified against bin/linux-amd64/daana-cli.sha256 before each invocation (engine.py:66) and I confirmed the committed pin actually matches the vendored binary (sha256sum -c returns OK).

subprocess.run in src/adss/destination.py:62 — argument list, no shell. notebook/shot/cache are Project paths; height is an int default; the only non-literal is str(height). env is os.environ plus PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=<repo>/.browsers.

destination.py:99-101 — shim() takes its build number from WANTED.search(marimo's stdout+stderr), which is subprocess output and therefore not fully trusted. But the pattern is r'chromium(?:_headless_shell)?-(\d+)' and group(1) is digits only, so the value can only produce a path segment like 'chromium-1234' inside <repo>/.browsers. No traversal, no argv, no execution — the symlink target comes from globbing /opt/pw-browsers, never from the output.

Fixture replay path traversal (src/adss/source.py:89-103) — replay() does (directory / name).read_bytes() where name comes from the manifest's 'requests' values, so a value of '../../../etc/x' would escape das/fixtures. I checked how those values are produced: record() (source.py:78-81) generates them itself as f'page-{len(requests):04d}.json' from a counter, and keys them by the locally-built page_url(). Nothing from the HTTP response — not the body, not a header, not the redirected URL — ever becomes a manifest value. Poisoning it therefore requires hand-editing a committed file under das/fixtures, which is repository content reviewed in a PR. Impact would also be limited to reading a file that happens to be valid OData JSON into the parquet lake, not execution.

urlopen host/protocol control (src/adss/source.py:52) — the URL is f'{service.rstrip("/")}/{entity}?$count=true&$top=...&$skip=...' with service and entity from das/contracts/*.yaml (repo content, https://demodata.grapecity.com/...). Nothing external picks the host or scheme. I checked redirect behaviour in the interpreter here (3.11.15): HTTPRedirectHandler.http_error_302 refuses any Location whose scheme is not http/https/ftp, so an upstream redirect cannot reach file:// and cannot become a local file read. A redirect to another http host would only change where response bytes come from — no credentials or headers are attached to the request, the body is used only as data, and the manifest is still keyed by the original URL. That is host-level SSRF with no sink, on a --live code path that is off by default.

yaml.load / unsafe deserialization — every YAML read is yaml.safe_load: contract.py:131, model.py:97, uss.py:89, mapping.py:51, question.py:63, engine.py:35. No yaml.load, no eval, no exec, no pickle, no dynamic import (the only importlib use is importlib.metadata.version in __init__.py; the two function-level imports, contract.py:165 and uss.py:133, are static module names).

SQL generation from outside the repository (src/adss/das.py, src/adss/uss.py) — I traced every interpolated value. das.py takes contract.table (a *.yaml filename stem), column.source_path/target_name/sql_type, and contract.primary_keys, all from das/contracts/*.yaml. uss.py takes entity/attribute/measure ids and types from dab/model.yaml and dab/uss.yaml. calendar_sql() is a constant. checks.py:68/78/83/96 interpolate entity.id from dab/model.yaml. Not one interpolated value originates in an HTTP response body, a fixture, or a filename from outside the repo. This is the 'a malicious contract could inject SQL' case the brief calls out, and I agree it is not a finding here: those files are PR-reviewed repository content, and whoever can edit them already gets arbitrary execution from the CI job that runs pytest and `adss build` on the PR's own code.

Landed data becoming SQL identifiers (src/adss/landing.py:30-45) — the dlt resource yields a fixed key set (payload, source_system, source_entity, source_url) with payload declared as a single json-typed column, so no key from an OData record is ever promoted to a column name, a child table, or a file path. The layout string uses only dlt's own placeholders ({table_name} = contract stem, {load_id}, {file_id}, {ext}).

platform.install() (src/adss/platform.py:105-110) splitting on ';\n' and executing each chunk — the only callers are cli.py:202 (a das/sql/*.sql file written seconds earlier in the same command from generated text) and cli.py:277 (the in-memory generated string, deliberately not the on-disk file). No external content reaches it.

sqlfluff.fix in src/adss/sqlformat.py:25 — the .sqlfluff config sets `templater = raw`, so no Jinja rendering happens over the generated SQL, and the input to formatted() is in any case generated only from repo YAML. library_path/macro loading would be config-driven, i.e. repo content.

engine.metadata_schema/is_installed (uncommitted work in src/adss/engine.py:33-52) — reads dab/connections.yaml with safe_load and passes the schema name as a bound parameter ('... WHERE table_schema = ?', [schema]), not by interpolation.

The absolute repo path embedded as a SQL string literal in raw_view_sql (das.py:47-49, read_parquet('{glob}')) — a checkout directory containing a single quote would break or inject into that statement. The path is the developer's own choice of checkout location (CI checks out under /home/runner/work/<repo>/<repo>), not something an attacker supplies, so I do not treat it as external data.

Project.discover() (project.py:21-26) walking up for pyproject.toml, which makes the engine binary and its .sha256 both come from whatever root it finds — running `adss` inside an untrusted tree would run that tree's bin/linux-amd64/daana-cli, since the pin file sits beside the binary and attests reproducibility rather than origin. That is the same exposure as running any dev tool (make, pre-commit, pytest) inside an untrusted checkout, and the brief treats CLI invocation context as trusted.

HTML injection into the marimo page (destinations/app.py:104-115) — mo.md renders raw HTML, and it interpolates a1['order_month'].min()/max(). I checked the question's uss.sql: order_month is cal.month_label, which calendar_sql() builds with strftime over a DATE, so it cannot carry markup. The one genuinely source-derived string, destination_country, reaches only n_unique() (an int), the Vega spec (SVG text), and mo.ui.table (React-escaped). Every other interpolation (q1.question, q1.persona, defined[token]) is repo YAML.

CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) — trigger is `pull_request`, not `pull_request_target`; no secrets are referenced; ${{ }} expansions appear only in a concurrency group and a cache key, never inside a `run:` body. The 'Read the engine pin' step pipes repo file content into $GITHUB_OUTPUT via command substitution (not shell re-evaluation); a multi-line .sha256 could add extra output lines, but the only consumer is the cache key, and a poisoned cache is caught by the subsequent `sha256sum -c` before the binary is executed. source.yml touches the network but only records fixtures and diffs them; it never commits or pushes.

Note on repository state: src/adss/cli.py, engine.py and project.py have uncommitted modifications (the dab_install idempotency work) that landed while I was reading; I re-read all three and this review covers the current working-tree content, not just HEAD.

result.lens: Supply chain and CI: the vendored daana-cli binary and its checksum pin (src/adss/engine.py, bin/linux-amd64/*), .github/workflows/ci.yml and source.yml, .pre-commit-config.yaml, pyproject.toml/uv.lock, and the engine's cwd=dab/ invocation.
consideredAndRejected: CHECKSUM ENFORCEMENT ON EVERY EXECUTION PATH -- verified, no bypass. /home/user/adss-2026-09-07/src/adss/engine.py:79 Engine.run() calls require_detached() then self.verify() before subprocess.run([str(self.binary), ...]). grep across src/, tests/, destinations/ and checks/ finds exactly one construction of Engine (src/adss/cli.py:67) and no other invocation of the binary anywhere -- no test, no marimo cell, no CI step executes bin/linux-amd64/daana-cli outside Engine.run. All three dab subcommands (install/deploy/execute) and `adss build` route through it. verify() also fails closed on every degenerate input: missing .sha256 -> FileNotFoundError, empty file -> IndexError on .split()[0], uppercase digest -> mismatch. There is no `skip_verify` flag, no env-var escape and no cached-result short circuit. The newly added is_installed()/metadata_schema() early-return in dab_install (src/adss/cli.py:213-219) skips the *invocation*, never the verification of an invocation that happens.

CI CACHE POISONING OF THE ENGINE -- structurally closed, twice. .github/workflows/ci.yml restores `bin/linux-amd64/daana-cli` from actions/cache@v4 under key `engine-${{ steps.engine.outputs.sha256 }}`, which is untrusted storage. But the very next step (`Check the pin`) runs `(cd bin/linux-amd64 && sha256sum -c daana-cli.sha256)` against the *committed* checksum file, and the cache `path:` covers only the binary -- the .sha256 is never restored from the cache, so a cache entry cannot supply a matching checksum for a substituted binary. `adss build` then verifies a second time in Python. Separately, the trust boundary that would matter does not exist: GitHub scopes caches per ref; fork `pull_request` runs write to an isolated `refs/pull/N/merge` scope that base-branch runs cannot read, and a same-repo branch push already implies write access. Making the key content-addressed rather than version-addressed is the right shape.

GITHUB_OUTPUT INJECTION VIA THE PIN FILE -- no target. `echo "sha256=$(cut -d' ' -f1 bin/linux-amd64/daana-cli.sha256)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"` would let a multi-line .sha256 forge additional step outputs. But (a) command substitution output is not re-evaluated as shell, so there is no command injection; (b) .sha256 is committed repository content, trusted per the stated model; (c) nothing in the job reads any output of that step except the cache key, and the cache key is then re-validated by sha256sum -c. Even a successful injection buys nothing.

TOCTOU BETWEEN verify() AND subprocess.run -- no privilege boundary crossed. src/adss/engine.py:79-83 hashes the file, closes it, then execs the path. Swapping the file in that window requires write access to the working tree, which is the same access that would let you edit engine.py itself, or Project.engine_binary, or any of the SQL the build runs. In CI the workspace is not shared with any other principal. Fixing this (exec via an open fd) would defend against nobody who is not already inside.

NON-CONSTANT-TIME CHECKSUM COMPARISON -- irrelevant by construction. `if digest != recorded` (src/adss/engine.py:71) compares two values that are both public: `recorded` is a plaintext file committed to the repository and mirrored in the git-LFS pointer. There is no secret, no remote attacker and no oracle to time -- a timing side channel would leak a value anyone can `cat`.

THE PIN PROVES INTEGRITY, NOT PROVENANCE -- real, but not an exploit, and already documented. verify() reads the expected digest from `self.binary.parent / f'{name}.sha256'`, i.e. from a file sitting beside the artefact it validates, so anyone who can replace the binary in the tree can replace the pin. The committed value 492ddf86... is also exactly the git-LFS pointer oid (git show HEAD:bin/linux-amd64/daana-cli), so LFS independently verifies the same digest on download and the two agree; I confirmed the on-disk 174 MB binary hashes to the recorded value. What neither pin establishes is that the blob was ever trustworthy -- there is no upstream-published checksum, signature or attestation to compare against. docs/adr/0004 states this in its own consequences ('The .sha256 proves it has not changed; it does not prove it was ever trustworthy'). That is a known, accepted gap, not a defect in this change.

source.yml TURNING A LIVE THIRD-PARTY RESPONSE INTO EXECUTION -- traced end to end, it cannot. The scheduled job runs `uv run adss das record`, then `git diff --exit-code -- das/fixtures`. In src/adss/source.py:record(), the response body is only json.loads'd and written verbatim; the filename is `page-{len(requests):04d}.json` (index-derived), the directory is `project.fixtures / contract.table` where table is Path.stem of a repo glob, and the manifest keys are URLs regenerated from the contract with an integer $skip. Nothing from the body reaches a filename, a path, a shell word or an eval, so there is no write outside das/fixtures. The `||` block's echoes are static literals. The response body does reach the runner's stdout through git diff, where `::`-prefixed lines are parsed as workflow commands -- but set-env/add-path were removed in 2020 and stdout save-state/set-output are disabled on current runners, leaving only log manipulation, which is out of scope. The job uses no secrets, makes no API call and never pushes; a human commits the diff.

THE SOURCE SERVER PIVOTING THE CLIENT TO ANOTHER HOST OR SCHEME -- closed by design. src/adss/source.py:pages() and record() both build every request from `page_url(endpoint, skip)` and deliberately never follow `@odata.nextLink` or any URL from the response, so a hostile OData service cannot redirect the fetcher at an internal host or a file:// path. urllib's default redirect handler additionally refuses non-http/https/ftp redirect targets. Endpoint.url is composed from contract YAML (service + entity), which is reviewed repository content -- a contract declaring `service: file:///...` is a repo-content change, out of scope by the stated trust model.

MALICIOUS CONTRACT / MODEL / MAPPING / QUESTION SQL INJECTING SQL OR PATHS -- explicitly considered and rejected per the stated trust model. das/contracts/*.yaml, dab/model.yaml, dab/uss.yaml, dab/mappings/*.yaml and docs/questions/**/{staged,uss}.sql are all reviewed repository content, and anyone who can change them already executes arbitrary code through the CI gate (pre-commit runs pytest). Contract-derived identifiers are interpolated unquoted into generated DDL in src/adss/das.py, and question SQL is executed verbatim in src/adss/checks.py and destinations/app.py -- both are repo-content-to-SQL, not external-data-to-SQL, so neither is a finding here. Every YAML load in the change uses yaml.safe_load (contract.py:131, model.py:97, mapping.py:51, uss.py:89, engine.py:35); none uses yaml.load or a full-constructor loader, so a YAML file cannot instantiate Python objects.

THE ENGINE'S cwd=dab/ CHANGING WHAT EXECUTES -- nothing writable from outside lands there. The engine is invoked with cwd=project.dab (src/adss/cli.py:69) and reads workflow.yaml, connections.yaml, model.yaml and mappings/*.yaml from it. connections.yaml declares only `type: duckdb` and `database: ../warehouse.duckdb` -- no extension repository, no plugin path, no hook command, nothing that names an executable or a fetch. No code in src/adss writes into dab/; the only files created there (model.json, workflow.compiled.json, mappings/*.json, logs/) are the engine's own output and are gitignored, so they are regenerated from the reviewed YAML on every CI run rather than carried in. External data reaches the engine only through the warehouse's das__staged views, as row values.

pre-commit HOOKS AS A FETCH-AND-EXECUTE SURFACE -- there is no fetch. Every hook is `repo: local` with `language: system` and an entry of the form `uv run --frozen <tool>`, so pre-commit clones and executes nothing from a remote tag; the tool versions are fixed by uv.lock. pre-commit passes filenames as argv rather than through a shell, so there is no word-splitting or command injection from a filename; a file named like a flag would need to be committed, which is repo content. The one hook worth naming is `pytest`, which means the CI gate job executes the PR's Python -- but that is inherent to running a test suite on a PR and is bounded by the `pull_request` event's read-only token and absent secrets (below).

UNTRUSTED PR CONTENT RUNNING WITH ELEVATED PRIVILEGE -- not present. grep over .github/workflows finds no `pull_request_target`, no `workflow_run`, no `issue_comment`, no `secrets.*` reference and no `environment:`. Triggers are `push: branches: ['**']`, `pull_request`, `schedule` and `workflow_dispatch` only. A fork `pull_request` run gets a read-only GITHUB_TOKEN and no secrets by default, so the arbitrary code it runs (pytest, `adss build`, the vendored binary) has nothing to steal or push to; a same-repo push already implies write access. There is no flow where fork content and repository credentials meet.

MUTABLE ACTION TAGS (actions/checkout@v5, actions/cache@v4, astral-sh/setup-uv@v7) -- real supply-chain exposure in principle, classified as missing hardening and excluded by the brief. Pinning to a commit SHA would be the standard mitigation; nothing about this change makes the exposure worse or concretely exploitable, since these jobs hold no secrets and a read-only token on the only untrusted-input path.

DEPENDENCY RESOLUTION -- uv.lock has 1729 hash entries, every `source` is `registry = "https://pypi.org/simple"` (plus one `editable = "."` for the project itself), and there is no git, URL, path or directory source. CI sets `UV_FROZEN: 1` and every install is `uv sync --all-groups --frozen` / `uv run --frozen`, so the resolution cannot drift at build time and artefacts are hash-verified.

setup-uv's OWN CACHE (enable-cache: true) -- unlike the engine cache this one has no post-restore verification, so a poisoned entry would deliver arbitrary wheels into the venv. Rejected for the same scoping reason: a fork PR writes to an isolated cache scope, and writing to the default branch's scope requires push access, which is already full trust. No cross-boundary path exists.

destination.py's BROWSER SHIM AND SUBPROCESS -- src/adss/destination.py:_capture() builds a fixed argv list (no shell), and shim() derives its path component from `WANTED = re.compile(r'chromium(?:_headless_shell)?-(\d+)')`, so group(1) is digits only and cannot traverse. The symlink targets come from a hardcoded /opt/pw-browsers glob, nothing is downloaded, and `adss shoot` is not invoked by either workflow.

EXTERNAL DATA RENDERED INTO THE MARIMO PAGE -- destinations/app.py interpolates warehouse-derived values into mo.md() f-strings, but only ints (total/months/countries, all wrapped in int() or n_unique()) and the min/max of order_month, a date-derived month key produced by the question's own SQL. Category values such as destination_country reach only Vega marks and mo.ui.table, which escape. Even granting a hostile OData response, there is no free-text field reaching the markdown renderer, and the page is a local developer artefact with no server. Not a supply-chain/CI concern and not concretely exploitable.

A DOC/TEST DISCREPANCY, NOTED NOT REPORTED: docs/adr/0004's Confirmation section claims 'tests/test_engine_pin.py asserts the binary's hash matches the committed .sha256', while that file's own docstring says the opposite ('The vendored binary itself is not hashed here'). The enforcement is real -- Engine.verify() at every invocation plus the CI `sha256sum -c` step -- so this is inaccurate documentation, not a missing control, and findings in docs and tests are out of scope.

result.lens: File handling and data exposure — path handling in project.py / source.py / destination.py / landing.py, writes and deletes outside the intended tree, injection into the rendered marimo page, and credential/PII handling in contracts, connections.yaml, fixtures and CI
consideredAndRejected: shim()'s build number is NOT a traversal vector. /home/user/adss-2026-09-07/src/adss/destination.py:19 compiles WANTED = re.compile(r"chromium(?:_headless_shell)?-(\d+)") and line 101 passes group(1) into cache / f"chromium_headless_shell-{build}". The capture is \d+, so it cannot contain a separator, a dot or a '..'. I confirmed empirically: 'chromium-../../x' does not match at all, and 'chromium-12/34' captures '12'. The symlink target side is also closed — _installed() only ever globs the image path /opt/pw-browsers, never anything derived from the subprocess output.

source.py record()'s `for stale in directory.glob("page-*.json"): stale.unlink()` (/home/user/adss-2026-09-07/src/adss/source.py:64-65) cannot be pointed outside das/fixtures by external data. `directory` is project.fixtures / read_contract(path).table (cli.py:111), and `table` is Path.stem of a das/contracts/*.yaml glob result — always a single filename component from the repository. No field of any HTTP response body reaches it. The only pathological case is a committed file named '...yaml', whose stem is '..' (verified), which would resolve the directory to das/ — but that requires committing that file, i.e. repository content, which this trust model treats as already trusted, and it still lands inside the repo. The glob is also restricted to page-*.json, so it cannot delete manifests or unrelated files.

replay() at /home/user/adss-2026-09-07/src/adss/source.py:91-103 reads (directory / name).read_bytes() where `name` comes from manifest.json's request index. A traversing value there would read outside das/fixtures — but record() only ever writes locally generated names (f"page-{len(requests):04d}.json", line 78); the URL is the key, never the value. The only way to get a traversing value into a manifest is to hand-edit committed repository content, and the result is fed to json.loads and then to the lake, not executed.

Contract / model / uss / mapping / question SQL injection — explicitly out of scope per the stated trust model, and I confirmed the mechanism exists so it is on record if the model ever changes: das.py:26 interpolates a contract's source_path into a '$.…' SQL string literal; das.py:45,67,70,91 and uss.py:165-207,241-255 emit target names, entity ids and attribute ids as bare or "-quoted identifiers with no escaping; checks.py:68,83,97 does the same with entity.id; cli.py:243,267 writes dar/uss/{entity.id.lower()}.sql. All of these are sourced from das/contracts/*.yaml, dab/model.yaml and dab/uss.yaml, which are reviewed repository content.

raw_view_sql() (/home/user/adss-2026-09-07/src/adss/das.py:43,52) interpolates the absolute lake path into read_parquet('{glob}') — a single quote in the checkout directory would break out of the literal into generated SQL that is then written to das/sql/*.sql and executed. This is the 'path from outside the repo' case, but the checkout directory is chosen by the developer or by GitHub (/home/runner/work/<repo>/<repo>, where repo names cannot contain quotes). No attacker chooses it, so it is a robustness wart rather than an exploit.

HTML/markdown injection into destinations/app.py. mo.md renders raw HTML, and a marimo page that ran attacker HTML would sit in the kernel's origin — so I traced every interpolated value at app.py:104-115. total is int(), months and countries are n_unique() integers, q1.question and q1.persona are question.md front matter (repo content), and a1["order_month"].min()/.max() resolve to _calendar.month_label, which uss.py:294 emits as strftime(d.date_key, '%Y-%m') over a generated DATE range — so it is always YYYY-MM regardless of what the source sends. destination_country is the one genuinely source-controlled string and it never reaches mo.md: it appears only in n_unique() (app.py:102), in the Altair spec (app.py:129-158, serialized as JSON and painted into SVG <text>; vega-tooltip escapes) and in mo.ui.table (app.py:188, JSON into a React component). There is no path from an OData response body to raw HTML on the page.

SSRF / redirect abuse in over_http (/home/user/adss-2026-09-07/src/adss/source.py:52-54). The URL is built entirely from the contract (page_url, line 28-30: endpoint.service + entity + $count/$top/$skip); no field of any response is ever fetched — paging is by $skip, and @odata.nextLink is never read — so a hostile response body cannot steer the crawler to a new host. urllib's HTTPRedirectHandler restricts redirect schemes to http/https/ftp, so a file:// redirect is refused. Contract-controlled schemes (e.g. service: file:///etc) are repository content. The stated exclusion for path-only SSRF applies on top of all this.

dlt landing paths (/home/user/adss-2026-09-07/src/adss/landing.py:24,30-53). LAYOUT is {table_name}/extracted_on={YYYY}-{MM}-{DD}/{load_id}.{file_id}.{ext} — every placeholder is loader-generated or the contract's table name; bucket_url is root.absolute().as_uri(). The record body goes into one column declared columns={"payload": {"data_type": "json"}}, so no key inside a response body can become a column name, a child table or a file name. Provenance columns are fixed literals plus contract values.

Subprocess argument injection. engine.py:82-88 passes only literal strings chosen in cli.py ('install', '--connection', 'dev', 'deploy', 'execute') plus '--no-tui'; destination.py:62-88 passes only project-derived paths and literals. Both use the list form with no shell=True. Nothing from an HTTP body, a fixture, or a query result reaches an argv anywhere in the diff.

Engine pin handling. Engine.verify() (/home/user/adss-2026-09-07/src/adss/engine.py:64-76) streams sha256 and compares against daana-cli.sha256 before every subprocess.run (line 80-82), and .github/workflows/ci.yml:63-66 verifies again with sha256sum -c after the cache restore, so a poisoned actions/cache entry fails before the binary executes — and the cache key is the recorded digest itself. The pin proves LFS transport integrity only (anyone who can change the binary can change the .sha256 beside it), but that is repository content by definition.

Credential handling. There is none to get wrong: dab/connections.yaml declares a single local DuckDB file (database: ../warehouse.duckdb) with no user, password or DSN, and the profile's shape is fine — the engine is invoked with cwd=project.dab (cli.py:69) so the relative path cannot resolve elsewhere. metadata_schema is passed to DuckDB as a bound parameter (engine.py:50-52), not interpolated. The contracts' ownership blocks carry a team name and prose only. The OData endpoint is unauthenticated. Nothing in src/, destinations/ or the workflows reads a token or secret.

PII in das/fixtures. The recordings are the public Northwind demo dataset served from demodata.grapecity.com — company names, ship addresses, and (in the untracked customers fixture) contact names, phone and fax. That is well-known synthetic sample data, not real personal data, and it is the committed artefact the whole offline build depends on by design (ADR 0003).

adss check echoing warehouse rows. checks.py:141-145 (_first_gap) puts actual row tuples into a failing finding, which cli.py:298 echoes into CI logs. This is deliberate — a check that says 'they disagree' without saying how is useless — and the rows are aggregates (month, country, count) of the public demo dataset. Not concretely exploitable here.

das unpack's orphan deletion (/home/user/adss-2026-09-07/src/adss/cli.py:181-189) removes files under <root>/checks that no contract generates. It is bounded to that one directory, matches only *.sql (checks/README.md survives), and unlink() on a symlink removes the link rather than its target. The paths it writes (cli.py:158, 168, 267) are all <root>/das/sql, <root>/checks and <root>/dar/uss with repo-derived stems.

Derived artefacts leaking into the repo. I verified with git check-ignore that warehouse.duckdb, das/lake/, das/sql/, .screenshots/, .browsers/, __marimo__/, .dlt/ and dab/mappings/*.json are all ignored — so the built warehouse, the parquet lake, and destinations/__marimo__/session/app.py.json (a marimo session cache that can embed rendered cell outputs, i.e. warehouse data) are not committed. git ls-files confirms only the LFS pointer, .sha256 and .version are tracked under bin/.

Workflow token exposure. Neither .github/workflows/ci.yml nor source.yml references a secret, and neither sets a top-level permissions: block. ci.yml runs on push/pull_request (fork PRs get a read-only GITHUB_TOKEN and no secrets); source.yml runs on schedule/dispatch on the default branch and is the only job touching the network. The hostile input it could receive — an OData response body — is written to das/fixtures and then diffed with git diff --exit-code; it is never executed, so there is no path from it to the token. A missing permissions: block is hardening, which is out of scope.

GITHUB_OUTPUT injection at .github/workflows/ci.yml:50 (echo "sha256=$(cut -d' ' -f1 bin/linux-amd64/daana-cli.sha256)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"). A multi-line .sha256 file would emit extra lines into GITHUB_OUTPUT, but that file is repository content and the job holds no secrets, so there is nothing to steer.

Deserialization. Every YAML read in the diff uses yaml.safe_load (contract.py:131, model.py:97, uss.py:89, mapping.py:51, question.py:63, engine.py:35) — no yaml.load anywhere.
